title: Saturated monomial blowup charts commute with free monoid products
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $P$ a fine commutative monoid with torsion-free group completion $G$, and $I\subseteq P$ a finitely generated nonempty ideal. Let $H=\mathbf N^r\oplus\mathbf Z^t$ for finite $r,t\geq0$, $Q=P\oplus H$, and $I_Q=I\times H$ [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup] [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. For $a\in I$ put $C_a=P[I-a]$. Inside $Q^{\rm gp}=G\oplus H^{\rm gp}$ one has
$$Q[I_Q-(a,0)]=C_a\oplus H,\qquad (C_a\oplus H)^{\rm sat}=C_a^{\rm sat}\oplus H.$$
Consequently the ordinary and normalized scheme blowup charts for the extended ideal $k[I_Q]$ are respectively $k[C_a]\otimes_k k[H]$ and $k[C_a^{\rm sat}]\otimes_k k[H]$. In particular the canonical map
$$k[C_a^{\rm sat}]\otimes_{k[P]}k[Q]\longrightarrow k[(Q[I_Q-(a,0)])^{\rm sat}]$$
is an isomorphism, sending $e^c\otimes e^{(p,h)}$ to $e^{(c+p,h)}$. These maps identify the saturated monoscheme blowup charts and the normalized scheme blowup charts with pullbacks of the corresponding charts for $P$. They commute with all monomial overlap localizations, the comparison maps to the base, and the torus coactions. They are compatible with identities and composites of free product extensions and their localizations.

source.place: VIII Remark 3.1.23, Lemma 3.2.17 and Corollary 3.2.18, pp.101,105; explicit product-chart and saturation argument supplied by an agent.

proof.text: Choose finite nonempty ideal generators $E$ of $I$, enlarging $E$ by the chosen $a\in I$ when necessary. Then $E\times\{0\}$ generates $I_Q$: $(b,h)=(e,0)+(p,h)$ whenever $b=e+p$. The generators of $Q[I_Q-(a,0)]$ are $Q$ and $(b-a,h)$ for $b\in I,h\in H$. Each belongs to $C_a\oplus H$. Conversely $Q$ contains $(p,0)$ and $(0,h)$, and the difference generators with $h=0$ include $(b-a,0)$. They generate $C_a\oplus H$, proving the first equality. The group completion is $G\oplus\mathbf Z^{r+t}$: every element is a difference of elements of $P\oplus H$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.19 and Remark 3.1.23, p.101; explicit additive generator calculation.

proof.text: For $(g,u)\in G\oplus\mathbf Z^{r+t}$, membership in $(C_a\oplus H)^{\mathrm{sat}}$ means that $ng\in C_a$ and $nu\in H$ for some integer $n>0$. The latter condition says the first $r$ integer coordinates of $nu$ are nonnegative, equivalently those of $u$ are nonnegative; the last $t$ are unrestricted. Thus $u\in H$ and $g\in C_a^{\mathrm{sat}}$. Conversely a witness $ng\in C_a$ and $u\in H$ give $n(g,u)\in C_a\oplus H$. This proves the saturation equality, including $r=0$ or $t=0$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17 and Remark 3.1.23, p.101; explicit coordinatewise root-saturation calculation.

proof.text: For either $M=C_a$ or $M=C_a^{\mathrm{sat}}$, define $k[M]\otimes_k k[H]\to k[M\oplus H]$ by $e^m\otimes e^h\mapsto e^{(m,h)}$. Finite-sum bilinear extension is well-defined by the tensor universal property. Its inverse is $e^{(m,h)}\mapsto e^m\otimes e^h$, extended $k$-linearly on the monomial basis. Both preserve multiplication and the unit, since addition is componentwise; both composites fix the respective monomial or pure-tensor generators. Hence these are $k$-algebra isomorphisms. In particular $k[Q]=k[P]\otimes_k k[H]$.

source.place: VIII 3.2.1--3.2.2, pp.103--104, and Remark 3.1.23, p.101; explicit finite-sum tensor calculation supplied by an agent.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-toric-blowup-chart-normalization] to $(P,I,E)$ and $(Q,I_Q,E\times\{0\})$. The second monoid is fine because $P$ and $H$ have finite generating sets and both embed in their group completions; its group completion is torsion free by Step 1. That lemma gives ordinary chart rings $k[C_a]$ and $k[C_a\oplus H]$ and normalized rings $k[C_a^{\mathrm{sat}}]$ and $k[C_a^{\mathrm{sat}}\oplus H]$, using Steps 1--2. Step 3 gives exactly the two asserted tensor descriptions. In particular both normalized chart monoids are fine. Enlarging $E$ as in Step 1 makes this argument valid for every $a\in I$.

source.place: VIII Lemma 3.2.17 and Corollary 3.2.18, p.105; normalization input isolated in the existing toric chart node.

proof.text:
Put $M=C_a^{\mathrm{sat}}$ and $B=k[M]\otimes_{k[P]}k[Q]$. The proposed map $F:B\to k[M\oplus H]$ sends $e^c\otimes e^{(p,h)}$ to $e^{(c+p,h)}$; the balancing relation holds because moving $e^{p_0}$ across the tensor adds $(p_0,0)$ on either side. Define $V(e^{(c,h)})=e^c\otimes e^{(0,h)}$ and extend $k$-linearly. Both maps preserve products and units. Then $FV(e^{(c,h)})=e^{(c,h)}$, while
$$VF(e^c\otimes e^{(p,h)})=e^{c+p}\otimes e^{(0,h)}=e^c\otimes e^{(p,h)}.$$
Pure tensors of monomials generate $B$, so $F,V$ are inverses. The affine-spectrum fibre-product theorem identifies $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with the pullback of the $M$-chart over $\operatorname{Spec}k[P]$ to $\operatorname{Spec}k[Q]$, including both projection maps. Taking $M=C_a$ gives the identical ordinary-chart argument.

source.place: VIII Remark 3.1.23, p.101, and 3.2.17--3.2.18, p.105; explicit inverse and scheme pullback verification supplied by an agent.

proof.text: For $M=C_a^{\mathrm{sat}}$, the amalgamated sum $M\oplus_P(P\oplus H)$ is $M\oplus H$. Indeed compatible homomorphisms $f:M\to N$ and $g:P\oplus H\to N$ have the unique extension $(c,h)\mapsto f(c)+g(0,h)$; it restricts to $g$ because $f(p)=g(p,0)$. Apply [lem-trf-affine-monoscheme-hom-universal] to any locally monoidal test space $(T,\mathcal A)$ and $N=\Gamma(T,\mathcal A)$. Naturality identifies pairs of maps to $A(M)$ and $A(Q)$ agreeing over $A(P)$ with these compatible homomorphisms, hence with the unique map to $A(M\oplus H)$. This is the categorical pullback property, including its projections. The same calculation with $M=C_a$ proves the unsaturated version. No sharpness of the test stalks is required.

source.place: VIII Lemma 3.1.8(i), p.99, and Remark 3.1.23, p.101; explicit amalgamated-sum universal property.

proof.text: For $a,b\in E$ the overlap denominator in the $a$-chart is $d=b-a$, which becomes $(d,0)$ in the product chart. The chart-normalization node gives these overlap localizations before and after normalization. The finite-saturation node gives $(C_a-S)^{\mathrm{sat}}=C_a^{\mathrm{sat}}-S$, so the saturated formulas use precisely the same denominators. The maps in Steps 3 and 5 send each denominator to the corresponding monomial, and their inverses do likewise, so on a localized monomial they send $e^x/(e^d)^n$ to the monomial with exponent equal to the image of $x-nd$. This proves commutation with overlap maps and all further monomial localizations, including base localizations. On the monoid side the identical formula is $x-nd\mapsto\phi(x)-n\phi(d)$. Thus the chart identifications glue by the tuple-of-compatible-sections definition of the blowups, and retain the asserted pullback comparisons on every chart.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17--3.1.23, p.101, and localization sentence in the proof of 3.2.17, p.105; explicit fraction formulas.

proof.text: The base map sends $e^{(p,h)}$ to $1\otimes e^{(p,h)}$, whose image under $F$ is $e^{(p,h)}$, proving compatibility over the base. For the torus with group $G\oplus H^{\mathrm{gp}}$, the tensor monomial $e^c\otimes e^{(p,h)}$ has total degree $(c,0)+(p,h)=(c+p,h)$; both routes through the coaction therefore give $e^{(c+p,h)}\otimes e^{(c+p,h)}$. Finite-sum extension proves the full coaction square. For another free factor $H'$, both the iterated comparison and the direct comparison send $e^c\otimes e^{(p,h)}\otimes e^{(p',u,h')}$ to $e^{(c+p+p',h+u,h')}$; both inverses are the corresponding monomial decompositions. For the identity extension ($H=0$), the comparison is $e^c\otimes e^p\mapsto e^{c+p}$, the canonical identity pullback map. These equalities hold on generators and hence on the rings, on monoids, and their associated spaces. Step 7's fraction formula gives the same equalities after any stated localization.

source.place: VIII Remark 3.1.23, p.101, and coaction convention 3.2.15, p.105; explicit degree, identity and composition calculations.
